# 11 Of: engineering context

11 Of is a custom football jersey storefront for the Brazilian market. Read
AGENTS.md before editing Next.js code. README.md contains setup instructions;
package.json and the application source are authoritative for implementation.

## Identity and interface

- Brand constants: src/lib/brand.ts
- Wordmark: src/components/loja/BrandMark.tsx
- Theme: src/app/globals.css, Tailwind CSS 4 and OKLCH tokens
- Motion: src/components/loja/animations/ and src/lib/fly-to-cart.ts
- Locale: Brazilian Portuguese; display currency: BRL
- Fonts: configured in src/app/layout.tsx

## Application map

- src/app/(loja)/: storefront, catalog, product detail, editorials and favorites
- src/app/checkout/: dedicated checkout without the storefront layout
- src/app/pedido/[id]/: PIX presentation and payment/delivery status
- src/app/admin/: login, order list and delivery management
- src/app/_actions/cart.ts: add, update and remove signed cart entries
- src/app/_actions/checkout.ts: validate, reserve stock, create order and charge
- src/app/_actions/pix.ts: payment polling and regeneration
- src/app/_actions/delivery.ts: admin login and delivery updates
- src/app/_actions/notify.ts: stock notification registration
- src/app/api/webhooks/pagnet/route.ts: payment transaction reconciliation
- src/lib/catalog.ts: product/variant queries and cart resolution
- src/lib/images.ts: product/editorial image classification
- src/lib/image-loader.ts: Supabase image transformation URLs
- src/lib/supabase/: SSR, browser and session-refresh clients
- src/proxy.ts: Supabase session refresh

## External database contract

The repository does not include SQL migrations, seeds or database policies.
These names are inferred from application calls, not verified database state.

Tables used by the application:
- products: published catalog, integer prices, image URLs and ordering
- product_variants: product relation, size and stock quantity
- orders: customer, shipping, payment and delivery state
- order_items: quantity, variant references and purchase-time snapshots
- webhook_events: event identity used for duplicate detection
- notify_waitlist: product and email registrations

RPCs used by the application:
- reserve_stock(p_variant_id, p_qty)
- release_stock(p_variant_id, p_qty)
- delete_pending_order(p_order_id)
- set_order_pix: see the current checkout and PIX actions for arguments
- webhook_mark_paid(p_order_id, p_paid_at)
- webhook_mark_failed(p_order_id, p_payment_status)
- admin_update_delivery: see the current delivery action for arguments

The current Supabase clients use NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY. No service-role
client exists in this checkout. Verify grants, row-level security and RPC
authorization in the actual database before exercising writes.

## Checkout and payments

1. Read and validate the signed cart cookie.
2. Resolve variants and current prices from Supabase.
3. Validate customer and address fields with Zod.
4. Request stock reservations through reserve_stock, releasing reservations
   on handled failure paths.
5. Insert an order and purchase-time item snapshots.
6. Call createPixCharge in src/lib/pagnet/client.ts.
7. Store PIX data through set_order_pix, clear the cart and redirect to the order.

PagNet uses HTTP Basic credentials on the server. Amounts remain integer cents
in its request builder. Without both credentials the client creates a mock
charge; this does not simulate a confirmed payment. Current expiry is one day.

The webhook path is /api/webhooks/pagnet. It parses a callback, inserts an event
record, retrieves the canonical transaction through the authenticated API,
checks the order reference and amount, then calls a database state transition.
This is not an HMAC webhook integration. Payment retry and recovery semantics
still need to be verified against the external database and provider.

## Cart and local preferences

- src/lib/cart.ts: HMAC-SHA256, HTTP-only cookie, 3,500-byte serialized limit,
  at most 20 lines and 10 units per line; production secret >= 32 characters.
- src/lib/personalization.ts: shared cart-line identity and name sanitization.
- src/lib/wishlist.ts: browser-local favorites.
- src/lib/recently-viewed.ts: browser-local product history.
- src/lib/favorite-team.ts: browser-local team choice.
- src/lib/checkout-draft.ts: checkout draft helpers.

## Configuration and checks

Use .env.example for current variable names. PAGUE_* and
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY belong to an earlier integration and are not consumed
by the current source. Never put payment or admin secrets in NEXT_PUBLIC_*.

Commands: npm run dev, npm run lint, npm run build, npm run start.

Validate responsive storefront layouts, cart behavior and the configured order
flow separately. A public page, successful build or mock QR does not demonstrate
payment settlement, inventory correctness or fulfillment readiness. Keep test
orders and integration checks isolated from real customer data and transactions.
